## Run one, read one

A command that takes a model file also takes the name of a bundled model, when no file of that name is there. `naga examples` lists the names; `--path` prints the folder the files are in, to read or copy one:

```console
naga examples
naga examples --path
```

Some models use submodels that came from the asset libraries of a separate product; the engine runs the submodels, and that product's artwork is not in the files.

Two worked examples take some of these models through a decision: [airport ground support](../worked-examples/airport-ground-support.md) and [a container terminal](../worked-examples/container-terminal.md).

## How the numbers are made

`tools/gen_engine_docs.py` runs every model and writes these pages: seed 0, the model's own run length and warm-up, and as many replications as the model itself asks for, at most 3. Each number is the mean over those replications, at three significant digits, with the half-width of its 95% Student-t interval when there is more than one replication. A test regenerates every page and compares, so a number here is what the engine gives, on the version these pages were built from. Few replications make wide intervals: these are illustrations, not results to cite. The models whose answer is known exactly are compared with it on [Reference models](../validation/reference-models.md).

The diagrams are the model's own blocks and links, written as Mermaid text. They are drawn by a script your browser loads from unpkg.com, the one request these pages make to another site; without it a diagram shows as its text. A model of stocks and flows or of agents alone has no blocks to draw.
